context.text:
Route-to-holder LoRA routing: BLIS's route-to-holder policy
(atantawi/inference-sim c9fb6038, tag lora-seams-2026-08-22), ported to
llm-d-router v0.11.0.

THE DECISION. For a request carrying adapter a, collect the pods whose GPU
slots hold a, in input order (sim/routing.go:277-282).
- If at least one exists, restrict the candidate set to them, then run the
  ordinary weighted scorers and picker over that set (sim/routing.go:283-296).
- If none exists, or the request is for the base model, run them over every
  pod (sim/routing.go:299-300).
The rule adds no score of its own (sim/routing.go:375-382). Whenever a holder
exists, the pick is a holder. Every scorer's min-max range is taken over the
restricted set only. The target matches this because filters run before
scorers.

REQUIRED SHAPE: a hard restriction of the candidate set, not a score.

The simulator reads residency exactly and live, pinned to Immediate
(sim/cluster/cluster.go:443-448). The target has no residency signal, so the
port keeps a per-pod MIRROR of the simulator's resident set:
- capacity-bounded LRU with reference-counted pins;
- eviction of the least-recently-used unpinned adapter when a load starts
  (sim/simulator.go:1073-1094);
- residency only once the load completes (sim/simulator.go:1165-1191);
- touch and pin at batch admission (sim/simulator.go:950-959), unpin at
  termination (sim/simulator.go:975-981).
The mirror is driven by requests this plugin routed. It is confirmed by a
successful response from the pod, or by the adapter appearing in that pod's
ActiveModels. algorithms/routetoholder.go states the full state machine and
is authoritative.

ELIMINATIONS (settled; they hold even if the placement below fails)
- A Scorer cannot carry the decision. Scores combine as a weighted sum
  (pkg/epp/scheduling/scheduler_profile.go:236-260), so a holder preference
  only biases the pick. lora-affinity-scorer is exactly that weaker form
  (pkg/epp/framework/plugins/scheduling/scorer/loraaffinity/lora_affinity.go:84-117).
- label-selector-filter ignores the request
  (pkg/epp/framework/plugins/scheduling/filter/bylabel/selector.go:81-91), so
  it cannot vary by adapter.
- WaitingModels is not residency: by its own field comment, vLLM fills it with
  the same adapters as ActiveModels
  (pkg/epp/framework/interface/datalayer/metrics.go:29-32).
- ActiveModels alone is a SUBSET of the holders. It is running adapters only
  (pkg/epp/framework/plugins/datalayer/extractor/metrics/extractor.go:249-256),
  so idle resident adapters are absent.
- The /v1/models listing is a SUPERSET of the holders. It lists every
  registered adapter, including ones evicted from GPU slots.
- No core modification is needed.

PLACEMENT (candidate). ONE plugin registration, ONE Go type, plugin type
"route-to-holder-filter". It implements:
- scheduling Filter
  (pkg/epp/framework/interface/scheduling/plugins.go:60-63)
- requestcontrol PreRequest
  (pkg/epp/framework/interface/requestcontrol/plugins.go:70-73)
- ResponseHeaderProcessor (:78-81 of the same file)
- ResponseBodyProcessor (:98-101 of the same file)
The four method names are distinct, so one type can implement all four.
Every configured plugin is added to request control under each request-control
interface it implements (cmd/epp/runner/runner.go:799,
pkg/epp/requestcontrol/request_control_config.go:108-134). Register it beside
lora-affinity-scorer's registration (cmd/epp/runner/runner.go:618).
The method sets were read but nothing was compiled. If this placement does not
hold, the eliminations still do; search within them, not among scorers.
The treatment profile places the filter first, then the stock queue-scorer 2,
kv-cache-utilization-scorer 2 and prefix-cache-scorer 3, and max-score-picker.
So the arm differs from baseline only by the filter (config.md section 8).
Plugin parameters: fallbackSlots 3 (equal to --max-loras), and baseModels
["ibm-granite/granite-3.3-2b-instruct"].
The mirror is shared across goroutines: Filter reads it on the request path
while the response hooks mutate it. Every access must hold one mutex.

DECLARED DEGRADATION (D1-D13). Each is stated in full, with its direction of
bias, in the header of algorithms/routetoholder.go. In brief:
- D1: traffic this replica did not route is invisible, so holding is
  overstated. Run ONE EPP replica.
- D2, D11: loads are confirmed late, by a successful response header or a
  sampled ActiveModels refresh, so holding is understated just after a load.
  Streaming is forced on only by --record-itl.
- D3, D4: eviction is committed at dispatch, pins are taken at dispatch, and
  the mirror touches at dispatch, response and refresh. Victim choice can
  differ from the simulator's when queues are non-empty.
- D5: the mirror assumes vLLM GPU slots are LRU and running_lora_adapters
  means running. Both were checked at vLLM v0.7.1 only and are CONFIRM against
  the deployed image (config.md section 4).
- D6: slot count comes from MaxActiveModels, falling back to fallbackSlots
  until vLLM emits the LoRA metric.
- D7: the stock scorer weights differ from the simulator's 2:1:1, and the
  prefix scorer is approximate. Expected neutral on these synthetic prompts.
- D8: ties rotate round-robin in max-score-picker; the simulator breaks them at
  random.
- D9: the utilization detector filter runs after this one and narrows within
  the holders.
- D10: the base model is recognized by parameter.
- D12: the mirror can briefly exceed capacity when every slot is pinned.
- D13: a pending load is cleared when its request aborts.

STATUS. No measurement backs this rule against another routing rule, and no
simulation uses this cell. The expected effect is a hypothesis with no margin:
fewer adapter loads and a lower per-adapter TTFT tail than baseline
(README.md "Pre-registered expectation").
